post.caption: Bulgari's name hides a Roman V. Sotirios Voulgaris was a Greek silversmith from Epirus. In 1884, he opened a shop on the Via Sistina in Rome. In Italy, the Greek name Voulgaris became Bulgari. In 1905, the family moved to Via dei Condotti 10. His sons Giorgio and Costantino helped grow the house. Serpenti, a snake bracelet watch, began in the late 1940s. Ancient Roman and Greek coins entered its jewelry in the 1960s. Look at the logo: BVLGARI, with a V where the U goes.
